title: Finite-diagonal hyper-Ext spectral sequence in the bounded-below second argument
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a small ringed site, with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$ and the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Use $D(\mathcal O)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], its standard cohomology and truncations [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $K,L\in D(\mathcal O)$ and integers $r,c$ satisfy $H^j(K)=0$ for $j>r$ and $H^j(L)=0$ for $j<c$. Put $\mathcal Ext^p_{\mathcal O}(K,F)=H^pR\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(K,F[0])$ for a module sheaf $F$ and any integer $p$. There is a spectral sequence of module sheaves [def-sp-spectral-sequence]
$$E_2^{p,q}(L)=\mathcal Ext^p_{\mathcal O}(K,H^qL)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad H^{p+q}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(K,L),$$
with $d_s$ of bidegree $(s,1-s)$. It is natural and additive in morphisms of $L$, including its abutment maps and filtrations. It vanishes outside $p\geq-r$, $q\geq c$. In total degree $n$ its abutment has a finite exhaustive separated filtration [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-convergence] with graded pieces $E_\infty^{p,n-p}$; only $c\leq q\leq n+r$ occur. In particular $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(K,L)$ has cohomology zero below $c-r$. No constructibility, finite Tor amplitude, or cohomological-dimension bound on the site is assumed.

source.place: Tag 015W, lemma-ss-filtered-derived: filtered-derived spectral-sequence method. The stated internal-Hom/Postnikov variant expands the passage from Ext continuity to representable sums in ILO XVII 10.1.1, proof p. 325; it is not a verbatim specialization of the ordinary left-exact-functor statement.

proof.text: Put $T^n(M)=H^nR\mathcal Hom(K,M)$. Apply [lem-per-rhom-local-cohomological-bound] to the given small ringed site and $K$. It supplies an additive homological $T^0$, its coherent shifts $T^n$, natural boundary maps, and $T^n(M)=0$ when $M\in D^{\ge b}$ and $n<b-r$. Thus the amplitude hypothesis used below holds for every integer $b$, and $T^n(L)=0$ below $c-r$.

Apply [lem-per-postnikov-additive-exact-couple] with $\mathcal A=\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and the functor of Step 1. Its terms are $D^{p,q}=T^{p+q}(\tau_{\le q}L)$ and $E_2^{p,q}=T^p(H^q(L)[0])=\mathcal Ext^p_{\mathcal O}(K,H^qL)$, with precisely the required differential bidegrees. This also supplies additive page maps for every morphism of $L$ and compatibility with canonical abutment maps and filtrations after any fixed first-index translation. In Lean, form the E2 spectral-sequence functor by restricting each page along the translation (p,q) ↦ (p+r,q); the restriction homology comparisons give its next-page isomorphisms. Conjugation by the page comparisons gives naturality and additivity, and the initial layer comparison followed by the coherent shift comparison gives the asserted E2 identification.

source.place: Tag 011Q, exact couples; extracted Steps 4–5 and 9.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-postnikov-finite-cutoff-abutment] to this couple, using Step 1's bound for all $b$ and the assumed $L\in D^{\ge c}$. It gives support $p\ge-r,q\ge c$ and identifies the reindexed canonical abutment $T^n(\tau_{\le n+r}L)$ with $T^n(L)$ by the natural inclusion. Its transported filtration is $F^pT^n(L)=\operatorname{im}(T^n(\tau_{\le n-p}L)\to T^n(L))$, finite exhaustive and separated, with graded pieces $E_\infty^{p,n-p}$. Only $c\le q\le n+r$ occur. The comparison is natural, so Step 2's additive maps on abutments, filtration steps and graded pieces transport to the actual $T^n(u)$ and their restrictions. This proves every asserted compatibility, including the empty range $n+r<c$. To verify coherence for the chosen late-page isomorphisms, first use stabilization to show that the limiting cycle subobject equals every sufficiently late finite cycle subobject. The comparison from limiting cycles to finite cycles is therefore an isomorphism. Cancel this map and the epimorphic cycle-to-page projection to prove the transition and naturality equations. Finite cycle maps are constructed inductively using the given kernel and homology squares. Transport filtration steps along the natural isomorphisms T^0(-[n]) ≅ T^n(-); uniqueness through monic inclusions proves additivity of restrictions, and uniqueness through cokernel projections proves additivity and naturality of graded maps.

This is not an application of a left-exact-functor spectral sequence to a complex first argument.
